system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: A square, with a triangle attached to each side. Each triangle shares a side with the square, shown with a dotted line.]
The shape shown above is cut out of cardboard. The triangle flaps are then folded up along the dotted lines until they touch the edges of the flaps next to them.

Complete the diagram below to show what the shape would look like when viewed from directly above.

[Image: A square.]

Figure, described in words:
Top diagram: A flat net composed of a central square with dashed sides, each side joined to the base of an identical isosceles triangle pointing outward.
Bottom diagram: A square drawn with solid lines, representing the outer border of the shape viewed directly from above, awaiting completion.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw the two diagonals of the square, from each corner to the centre, as solid lines meeting at the centre point. The outer square stays the same size, because the base of the pyramid is the original square. The folded triangles meet above the centre to form a square pyramid, so from directly above the four slanted edges run from the apex at the centre to the four corners of the square.
